You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To build a wall made of beer bottles, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Apply final sealant to the exterior bottle faces (4 hours)
Step 2. Sort collected bottles by color and size (3 hours)
Step 3. Calculate the weight distribution for the upper section (1 hour)
Step 4. Install decorative LED backlighting behind the glass (2 hours)
Step 5. Soak bottles in warm soapy water (1 hour)
Step 6. Research historical bottle wall patterns (2 hours)
Step 7. Scrub stubborn residue from bottle interiors (2 hours)
Step 8. Dry bottles thoroughly using a compressed air hose (30 minutes)
Step 9. Purchase heavy-duty cleaning brushes (45 minutes)
Step 10. Polish the glass to a high shine (1 hour)
Step 11. Lay the first course of bottles in the mortar (5 hours)
Step 12. Measure the total length of the intended wall (30 minutes)
Step 13. Source 500 empty glass bottles from local recycling (3 days)
Step 14. Rinse bottles to remove sugar and yeast (1 hour)
Step 15. Draft a blueprint for the bottle arrangement (2 hours)
Step 16. Select the most transparent bottles for eye-level rows (1 hour)
Step 17. Organize the bottles into crates by height (1 hour)
Step 18. Clear the workspace of debris (1 hour)
Step 19. Mark the wall's footprint on the ground (20 minutes)
Step 20. Dig a shallow trench for the foundation (4 hours)
Step 21. Sift sand for a fine mortar mix (1 hour)
Step 22. Buy bags of Portland cement (1 hour)
Step 23. Inspect bottles for cracks or chips (2 hours)
Step 24. Set up a temporary support frame (3 hours)
Step 25. Install vertical rebar for reinforcement (2 hours)
Step 26. Mix a small test batch of mortar (30 minutes)
Step 27. Pour the concrete footer (6 hours)
Step 28. Take a photo of the sorted inventory (10 minutes)
Step 29. Apply mortar to the bottle bases (5 hours)
Step 30. Level the ground inside the trench (2 hours)
Step 31. Build a sturdy wooden mixing trough (2 hours)
Step 32. Lubricate the cement mixer (15 minutes)
Step 33. Purchase safety goggles and gloves (30 minutes)
Step 34. Arrange bottles on a tarp to visualize the pattern (2 hours)
Step 35. Scrape off remaining paper labels (3 hours)
Step 36. Cut the necks off select bottles for custom fits (4 hours)
Step 37. Stack the second course of bottles (5 hours)
Step 38. Fill gaps between bottles with small glass shards (3 hours)
Step 39. Install a top plate to stabilize the structure (3 hours)
Step 40. Rent a professional grade cement mixer (1 hour)
Step 41. Buy specialized glass-cleaning solution (20 minutes)
Step 42. Measure the height of the first row (15 minutes)
Step 43. Transport cement bags to the build site (1 hour)
Step 44. Design a rain-cap for the top of the wall (2 hours)
Step 45. Lay the third course of bottles (5 hours)
Step 46. Set up a string line for level accuracy (30 minutes)
Step 47. Pour a gravel sub-base (3 hours)
Step 48. Lay the fourth course of bottles (5 hours)
Step 49. Tape the bottle openings to keep mortar out (2 hours)
Step 50. Attach the rain-cap to the top course (2 hours)
Step 51. Inspect the mixer for any defects (15 minutes)
Step 52. Compact the soil at the bottom of the trench (1 hour)
Step 53. Collect cardboard for bottle protection (1 hour)
Step 54. Grout the joints between the bottles (6 hours)
Step 55. Purchase a masonry trowel (20 minutes)
Step 56. Sharpen the masonry chisel (15 minutes)
Step 57. Remove labels using a heat gun (2 hours)
Step 58. Clean the workspace of mortar splashes (2 hours)
Step 59. Let the mortar cure for the first 24 hours (24 hours)
Step 60. Sort bottles by glass thickness (1 hour)
Step 61. Remove any remaining adhesive with Goo Gone (2 hours)
Step 62. Wipe down the bottles with a microfiber cloth (1 hour)
Step 63. De-rim the bottle edges (2 hours)
Step 64. Buy a pallet of sand (1 hour)
Step 65. Stake out the corners of the wall (1 hour)
Step 66. Level the foundation surface (2 hours)
Step 67. Brush away excess dry mortar (1 hour)
Step 68. Sketch the structural load points (1 hour)
Step 69. Wash the mixing tools (30 minutes)
Step 70. Organize bottles by color gradient (2 hours)
Step 71. Scout a flat location for the wall (2 hours)
Step 72. Sanitize the bottles (1 hour)
Step 73. Inventory the different bottle brands (1 hour)
Step 74. Apply a second layer of mortar for stability (4 hours)
Step 75. Measure the diameter of each bottle neck (1 hour)
Step 76. Point the mortar joints for a finished look (4 hours)
Step 77. Soak labels in a vinegar solution (2 hours)
Step 78. Test the mortar's consistency (15 minutes)
Step 79. Buy a spirit level (15 minutes)
Step 80. Wet the foundation to improve mortar bonding (30 minutes)
Step 81. Dry-fit the bottles into the pattern (3 hours)
Step 82. Assemble the scaffolding (3 hours)
Step 83. Tamp down the gravel base (1 hour)
Step 84. Calibrate the laser level (20 minutes)
Step 85. Group bottles by their height (1 hour)
Step 86. Buy a bulk supply of water for mixing (1 hour)
Step 87. Mix the main batch of mortar (45 minutes)
Step 88. Cut rebar to the appropriate height (2 hours)
Step 89. Lay the fifth course of bottles (5 hours)
Step 90. Lay the sixth course of bottles (5 hours)
Step 91. Smooth the mortar joints with a striking tool (3 hours)
Step 92. Build a protective canopy over the wall (4 hours)
Step 93. Reinforce the corners with larger bottles (3 hours)
Step 94. Check the wall for plumbness (30 minutes)
Step 95. Fill the bottle interiors with colored sand (4 hours)
Step 96. Buff the bottle bottoms (1 hour)
Step 97. Inspect the bottles for air bubbles (1 hour)
Step 98. Purchase a diamond-blade glass saw (1 hour)
Step 99. Rent a van for bottle transport (2 hours)
Step 100. Call the local utility line to check for pipes (1 hour)
